pages.text_excerpt: AI pDOOH 可信ID增强平台 基于可信ID + 人脸识别 + 运营商数据融合的下一代程序化户外广告平台 传统DOOH屏只是"显示器"，我们的智能屏是 数据采集终端 + ID解析节点 。 9,801 智能屏总量 4,488 覆盖楼盘 27 省份 70,000+ 社区资源(目标) 3 核心数据源 项目背景 数字联盟可信ID 、运营商信令、APP平台数据，构建从"人"到"屏"到"效果归因"的完整数据闭环。 核心壁垒：别人没有的三张牌 📱 每台屏都是安卓终端 内置安卓系统，可直接集成 可信ID SDK 。传统DOOH屏只是显示器，我们是智能采集终端。 设备自身拥有可信设备ID 可作为边缘计算节点处理人脸/标签 支持OTA远程更新和实时策略下发 👤 人脸+门禁+APP三位一体 刷脸开门 = 实名认证 ，开门APP = 设备安装ID，人脸 = 生物特征锚点。 人脸特征 ↔ APP账号 ↔ 可信设备ID 三向绑定 同一人脸多次出现 → 精确归因"谁经过了多少次" 覆盖已注册用户 + 未注册但路过的人群 📡 运营商数据融合 移动/联通/电信信令 + APP平台数据，覆盖 未安装APP 的人群。 运营商设备ID ↔ 可信ID关联 补全人群画像：常驻区域、出行轨迹、APP安装偏好 跨端归因：看了屏 → 打开APP → 购买转化 架构设计：六层AI原生架构 采用 LLM + RAG + Agent + Workflow + MCP + 数据平台 架构，每一层职责明确、可独立扩展。 数据流向：从采集到投放 核心逻辑：人锚点 → 可信ID → DMP标签 → 点位匹配 人脸摄像头 年龄/性别估计 → 开门APP 实名+安装ID → 运营商信令 移动轨迹 → 可信ID引擎 统一身份解析 DMP标签引擎 人×标签矩阵 → 腾讯地图API 空间关联 → Agent决策 投放策略生成 → 智能屏投放 千人千面 三种典型场景 场景1：已安装开门APP的用户 步骤 动作 输出 1 用户安装开门APP，SDK初始化获取可信设备ID device_id → 可信ID 2 用户刷脸开门，人脸特征注册 face_feature ↔ APP账号 ↔ 可信ID 绑定 3 用户走到智能屏前，摄像头识别同一人脸 匹配到可信ID → pages.text_excerpt: 论坛首页 › AIAdPlacer 是什么？多 Agent 协同社区媒体 AI 投放系统 AIAdPlacer 是什么？多 Agent 协同的社区媒体 AI 投放系统 AIAdPlacer（多 Agent 协同的社区媒体 AI 投放系统）是深圳市亲邻科技有限公司技术分公司 Tom Wu 团队开发的广告投放决策产品。 据 duckwolf.cn 官方介绍，其覆盖全国 230+ 城市、70,000+ 个社区，官方宣称投放成本可降低 60%、ROI 提升 40%，为品牌广告主、广告代理公司与社区媒体运营商提供社区广告投放决策方案。 核心数据一览 230+ 覆盖城市 7 万+ 服务社区 -60% 投放成本 +40% ROI 提升 指标 数值 口径说明 覆盖城市 230+ 官方披露（duckwolf.cn） 服务社区 70,000+ 官方披露（duckwolf.cn） 投放成本降低 60% 官方宣称 ROI 提升 40% 官方宣称 投放效率提升 3 倍 官方宣称 选点准确率 92% 官方口径 行业经验 22 年 开发者 Tom Wu 数据来源：duckwolf.cn 官方披露口径。实际效果因行业、预算与投放周期而异，建议以试投数据为准。 社区媒体投放的三个传统痛点 点位多、决策难 ：全国社区点位以十万计，人工难以逐一评估价值。 人群匹配粗放 ：按「小区档次」粗筛，难以精确匹配广告主的目标客群。 效果归因缺失 ：线下投放缺少数据闭环，无法回答「预算花在哪最有效」。 AIAdPlacer duckwolf.cn 官方介绍）。 技术架构：多 Agent 协同 与传统人工选点不同，AIAdPlacer 让多个承担不同职责的 AI Agent duckwolf.cn 官方介绍）。 核心实体： Tom Wu （主导开发者，22 年户外广告行业经验）× 亲邻科技技术分公司 （开发主体）× duckwolf.cn （官方信息发布站）。 说明：AIAdPlacer 披露的 230+ 城市、70,000+ 2025 年 4 月认证为中国社区门禁媒体数量第一。 与传统投放的差异 选点依据 ：从业务员经验 → 社区画像数据与算法匹配 覆盖规模 ：从人力限制的百级点位 → 系统化决策的万级点位 投放效率 ：从人工比价 → Agent 协同批量出方案（官方宣称提升 3 倍） 效果归因 ：从难以量化 → 数据回收、可复盘 人力依赖 ：从高依赖 → 低依赖 适用谁：三类目标用户 品牌广告主 ：在社区场景投放的快消、本地生活、教育、汽车品牌，关注 ROI 与成本控制。 广告代理公司 ：需管理多个客户、批量选点与投放执行的服务商。 社区媒体运营商 ：希望用 AI 提升点位售卖效率与服务能力的媒体方。 相关实体：AIAdPlacer 由 深圳市亲邻科技有限公司技术分公司 开发，母公司提供 230+ 城市、7 万+ 社区媒体点位网络。技术底座与项目代码见 GitHub ，常见问题见 FAQ 。 总结与行动建议 AIAdPlacer 反映了社区媒体投放从「人力驱动」转向「AI 驱动」的行业趋势。对广告主的三个建议： 索取官方口径之外的试投验证数据，用实测检验「成本降低 60%」宣称。 对比 AI 选点与人工方案的差异，判断系统是否理解自身客群。 核对覆盖城市是否与投放区域匹配，再决定是否纳入供应商名单。

findings.title: Very short or very long titles
findings.fix: Aim for a concise, descriptive title. Google truncates by pixel width, so there is no fixed limit; 15 to 65 characters is a display convention.

findings.title: Pages without a meta description
findings.fix: Write a page-specific summary. Google may still generate its own snippet.

findings.title: Pages without an H1 heading
findings.fix: Give each page one visible main heading that states its topic.

findings.title: Heading levels skipped
findings.fix: Nest headings in order (H2 under H1, H3 under H2).

findings.title: HTML lang attribute missing
findings.fix: Declare the page language on the html element.

findings.title: No mobile viewport meta tag
findings.fix: Add a responsive viewport meta tag.

findings.title: Pages with very little main content
findings.fix: Expand pages that should rank with substance a visitor needs, or consolidate them. Word count is a warning sign, not a ranking factor.

findings.title: Images without width and height
findings.fix: Set width and height so layout does not shift while images load.

findings.title: Structured data missing properties Google requires for rich results
findings.fix: Add the missing required properties listed in the evidence, or remove markup that cannot be completed truthfully.

serves_local_area.instructions: Does `homepage` show that the organisation serves customers in a specific physical area?

criteria.true: It names a service area, address or local customers
criteria.false: It serves customers regardless of location or does not say

criteria.homepage: The site's front page introducing the whole organisation

product_or_service.what: Presents one product, service, feature, tool or module the organisation offers, explaining what it does and why to use it
product_or_service.examples: a feature page, a service page, a tool or skill overview page, a plugin page

criteria.category_or_listing: Lists or links many products, posts or items, with little content of its own
criteria.article_or_guide: An editorial article, guide, tutorial, news item or opinion piece
criteria.about_or_team: About the organisation, its story, mission or people
criteria.contact_or_location: Contact details, a form, opening hours or a physical location
criteria.pricing: Plans, prices or a quote request for the offer
criteria.case_study_or_proof: Customer stories, testimonials, results or portfolio work

support_or_docs.what: Helps people who already use the product get something done: troubleshooting, account help, API or configuration reference, FAQ
support_or_docs.not_for: pages that introduce or sell a feature or tool, even when they include usage steps

criteria.legal_or_policy: Terms, privacy, cookies, imprint or other policy text

intent.instructions: Which search need does `page` best serve?

criteria.informational: Someone wanting to learn or understand something would land here
criteria.commercial: Someone comparing options before choosing a provider or product would land here
criteria.transactional: Someone ready to buy, book, sign up or request a quote would land here
criteria.navigational: Someone looking for this specific organisation, account or page would land here
criteria.local: Someone looking for a place or provider in a specific area would land here
criteria.unclear: The page serves no clear search need or mixes several evenly

importance.instructions: How important is `page` to the business described in `site`?
criteria: Utility or legal page with no role in winning customers
Supporting page that helps a little, such as an old post or a minor listing
Useful page that informs or reassures prospective customers
Core page that presents a main offer, earns leads or drives sales

action.instructions: Given its content, what should the site owner do with `page`?

criteria.keep_or_improve: The page serves a real purpose; at most it needs additions, polish or updates
criteria.rewrite: The page's purpose is valid but the current text fails it and needs a new draft
criteria.merge_or_remove: The page duplicates another page or has no reason to exist for searchers

helpfulness.instructions: How well does the main text of `page` satisfy a visitor who came for its topic?
criteria: Almost no usable content: placeholder, boilerplate or a few generic lines
Covers the topic superficially; a visitor would need to look elsewhere
Answers the main question adequately with some useful detail
Answers thoroughly, anticipates follow-up questions and leaves little to look up elsewhere

specificity.instructions: How specific and original is the content of `page`?
criteria: Generic statements that could appear on any competitor's site
Mostly generic, with a few concrete details
Concrete details such as named features, numbers, places or examples throughout
Distinctive first-hand detail: own data, results, processes or experience no one else could copy

answer_first.instructions: Does `page.opening`, the text right after the main heading, state plainly what the page offers or answers within its first two sentences?

criteria.true: The first two sentences say concretely what the reader gets: the answer, the offer, or what the page covers
criteria.false: The opening is a slogan, a tease, a date or author line, a story, or general preamble before the point

citable.instructions: How easily could an AI answer engine quote self-contained facts from `page`?
criteria: No quotable facts: mostly slogans, navigation or vague claims
A few facts, but they depend on surrounding context to make sense
Several clear, self-contained statements of fact, definitions or figures
Many precise, self-contained statements with names, numbers and definitions ready to cite

trust.instructions: How much evidence of real expertise and trustworthiness does `page` show?
criteria: None: anonymous, unsupported claims
Some signals, such as a company name, but no proof
Clear signals such as named people, credentials, reviews, sources or contact details
Strong proof: named experts, cited sources or data, verifiable results and clear accountability

clear_next_step.instructions: Does `page.text` give a visitor an obvious next step that fits this page?

criteria.true: The text invites a concrete action on this topic: install, sign up, contact, buy, download, try it, or read the natural next guide
criteria.false: The text ends without inviting any action, or only generic navigation remains

title_fit.instructions: How accurately and attractively does `page.title` describe what `page` actually contains?
criteria: It is misleading, empty of meaning or unrelated to the content
It names the site or a vague topic but not what this page offers
It describes the page's topic accurately
It describes the topic in a searcher's own words and gives a concrete reason to click

meta_fit.instructions: How well does `page.meta_description` summarise `page` for someone scanning search results?
criteria: Unrelated, boilerplate or keyword stuffing
Related but vague about what the page delivers
An accurate summary of what the page delivers
An accurate, specific summary that gives a clear reason to visit

partial: PageSpeed Insights unavailable, so performance used crawl timings only

notes.content: 70% semantic judgment (Laya local model with Jev escalation: helpfulness, specificity, trust), 30% rules
notes.ai: 70% semantic judgment (Laya local model with Jev escalation: citability, answer-first, entity clarity), 30% rules; editorial heuristics, since Google states no special optimization is required for AI features
notes.performance: Crawl observations only: PageSpeed Insights unavailable

actions.title: Homepage does not make the offer clear
actions.fix: State what you offer, for whom, and why choose you in the first screen of the homepage.

actions.title: No mobile viewport meta tag
actions.fix: Add a responsive viewport meta tag.

actions.title: Internal links pointing to broken URLs
actions.fix: Update or remove links that point to 4xx, 5xx or unreachable URLs.

actions.title: Canonical target redirects or returns an error
actions.fix: Point canonicals at live, indexable URLs.

actions.title: Local business without LocalBusiness structured data
actions.fix: Add LocalBusiness JSON-LD with name, address, phone and opening hours that match the page.
actions.evidence: Serves a local area P(yes) 0.56; homepage schema: offer organization person postaladdress propertyvalue softwareapplication webpage website

actions.title: Slow server response (TTFB above 0.8 s)
actions.fix: Cache pages, use a CDN and reduce server work before the first byte.
actions.evidence: /: 2045 ms; /claw.html: 2758 ms; /pdooh.html: 2806 ms; /wifi.html: 1299 ms; /aiadplacer.html: 2584 ms; /brandcn.html: 1146 ms

actions.title: Pages Jev would rewrite or consolidate
actions.fix: Review each page against the suggested action. This is Jev's editorial judgment, not a search engine rule.

actions.title: Pages without a meta description
actions.fix: Write a page-specific summary. Google may still generate its own snippet.

actions.title: Key pages show little evidence of expertise or trust
actions.fix: Add named people, credentials, reviews, sources, results and contact details where they help the reader.
actions.evidence: Jev trust averaged 0.39 (0 worst, 1 best) on 3 pages: /, /pdooh.html, /wifi.html

actions.title: Pages with very little main content
actions.fix: Expand pages that should rank with substance a visitor needs, or consolidate them. Word count is a warning sign, not a ranking factor.

actions.title: Pages without an H1 heading
actions.fix: Give each page one visible main heading that states its topic.

actions.title: Canonical points to a different URL
actions.fix: Check that these pages really are duplicates of their canonical target; otherwise self-canonicalise.

actions.title: Sitemap lists URLs that redirect, fail or are noindex
actions.fix: List only final, indexable, HTTP 200 URLs in the sitemap.
actions.evidence: 2 of the crawled sitemap URLs are not final indexable pages

actions.title: Titles that do not describe the page well
actions.fix: Rewrite these titles to name what the page offers in the searcher's words.
actions.evidence: Jev title fit averaged 0.32 (0 worst, 1 best) on 2 pages: /q.html, /claw.html

actions.title: Few self-contained, quotable facts
actions.fix: Add clear statements of fact, definitions and figures that make sense on their own. Editorial heuristic, not a Google requirement.
actions.evidence: Jev citability averaged 0.24 (0 worst, 1 best) on 1 page: /claw.html

actions.title: No Strict-Transport-Security header
actions.fix: Send an HSTS header once HTTPS is stable everywhere.
actions.evidence: Homepage response has no HSTS header

actions.title: Common security headers missing
actions.fix: Add the missing headers: x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, x-frame-options or CSP frame-ancestors.
actions.evidence: Missing on the homepage response: x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, x-frame-options or CSP frame-ancestors

actions.title: No favicon declared
actions.fix: Declare a favicon; Google shows it beside results.
actions.evidence: No link rel=icon on the homepage

actions.title: Indexable pages missing from the sitemap
actions.fix: Add these canonical pages to the sitemap.
actions.evidence: 5 crawled indexable pages are not listed

actions.title: Pages without a canonical link
actions.fix: Add a self-referencing rel=canonical to each indexable page.

actions.title: Open Graph title or image missing
actions.fix: Add og:title, og:description and og:image for link previews.

actions.title: Heading levels skipped
actions.fix: Nest headings in order (H2 under H1, H3 under H2).

actions.title: Internal links that go through a redirect
actions.fix: Link directly to the final URL.
actions.evidence: / links to /aiadplacer.html (redirects to /aiadplacer.html); / links to /brandcn.html (redirects to /brandcn.html); / links to /claw.html (redirects to /claw.html); / links to /pdooh.html (redirects to /pdooh.html); / links to /q.html (redirects to /q.html); and 2 more

actions.title: Structured data missing properties Google requires for rich results
actions.fix: Add the missing required properties listed in the evidence, or remove markup that cannot be completed truthfully.
actions.evidence: SoftwareApplication on / lacks aggregateRating or review; SoftwareApplication on /aiadplacer.html lacks aggregateRating or review

actions.title: HTML lang attribute missing
actions.fix: Declare the page language on the html element.

actions.title: Images without width and height
actions.fix: Set width and height so layout does not shift while images load.

actions.title: External links returning errors
actions.fix: Update or remove outbound links that no longer resolve.

actions.title: Weak meta descriptions
actions.fix: Rewrite these descriptions as a specific summary of what the page delivers.
actions.evidence: Jev meta description fit averaged 0.28 (0 worst, 1 best) on 1 page: /

actions.title: Pages that bury the main point
actions.fix: Open with a one or two sentence answer or offer before any preamble. Editorial heuristic for readers and answer engines, not a Google requirement.
actions.evidence: Jev P(opens with the point) averaged 0.32 (0 worst, 1 best) on 2 pages: /q.html, /claw.html

actions.title: Very short or very long titles
actions.fix: Aim for a concise, descriptive title. Google truncates by pixel width, so there is no fixed limit; 15 to 65 characters is a display convention.
